studies.title: Prolonged stimulation of growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor I secretion by CJC-1295, a long-acting analog of GH-releasing hormone, in healthy ad
studies.abstract:
Context

Therapeutic use of GHRH to enhance GH secretion is limited by its short duration of action.

Objective

The objective of this study was to examine the pharmacokinetic profile, pharmacodynamic effects, and safety of CJC-1295, a long-acting GHRH analog.

Design

The study design was two randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, ascending dose trials with durations of 28 and 49 d.

Setting

The study was performed at two investigational sites.

Participants

Healthy subjects, ages 21-61 yr, were studied.

Interventions

CJC-1295 or placebo was administered sc in one of four ascending single doses in the first study and in two or three weekly or biweekly doses in the second study.

Main outcome measures

The main outcome measures were peak concentrations and area under the curve of GH and IGF-I; standard pharmacokinetic parameters were used for CJC-1295.

Results

After a single injection of CJC-1295, there were dose-dependent increases in mean plasma GH concentrations by 2- to 10-fold for 6 d or more and in mean plasma IGF-I concentrations by 1.5- to 3-fold for 9-11 d. The estimated half-life of CJC-1295 was 5.8-8.1 d. After multiple CJC-1295 doses, mean IGF-I levels remained above baseline for up to 28 d. No serious adverse reactions were reported.

Conclusions

Subcutaneous administration of CJC-1295 resulted in sustained, dose-dependent increases in GH and IGF-I levels in healthy adults and was safe and relatively well tolerated, particularly at doses of 30 or 60 microg/kg. There was evidence of a cumulative effect after multiple doses. These data support the potential utility of CJC-1295 as a therapeutic agent.

studies.title: Pulsatile secretion of growth hormone (GH) persists during continuous stimulation by CJC-1295, a long-acting GH-releasing hormone analog.
studies.abstract:
Context

Pulsatile GH secretion is considered important for many of the hormone's physiological effects. Short-term GHRH infusions enhance GH pulsatility and increase IGF-I, but the short GHRH half-life limits its therapeutic use. A synthetic GHRH analog (CJC-1295) that binds permanently to endogenous albumin after injection (half-life = 8 d) stimulates GH and IGF-I secretion in several animal species and in normal human subjects and enhances growth in rats.

Objective

Our objective was to assess GH pulsatility after a single injection of CJC-1295 and determine which GH secretion parameters correlated to the increase in IGF-I production.

Methods

GH pulsatility was assessed by 20-min blood sampling during an overnight 12-h period in healthy 20- to 40-yr-old men before and 1 wk after injection of either 60 or 90 microg/kg CJC-1295.

Results

GH secretion was increased after CJC-1295 administration with preserved pulsatility. The frequency and magnitude of GH secretory pulses were unaltered. However, basal (trough) GH levels were markedly increased (7.5-fold; P < 0.0001) and contributed to an overall increase in GH secretion (mean GH levels, 46%; P < 0.01) and IGF-I levels (45%; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between the responses to the two drug doses. The IGF-I increases did not correlate with any parameters of GH secretion.

Conclusions

CJC-1295 increased trough and mean GH secretion and IGF-I production with preserved GH pulsatility. The marked enhancement of trough GH levels by continuous GHRH stimulation implicates the importance of this effect on increasing IGF-I. Long-acting GHRH preparations may have clinical utility in patients with intact pituitary GH secretory capability.

studies.title: Once-daily administration of CJC-1295, a long-acting growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) analog, normalizes growth in the GHRH knockout mouse.
studies.abstract: Although the majority of children with isolated growth hormone (GH) deficiency have a good growth response to GH-releasing hormone (GHRH), the use of this therapeutic agent is limited by its very short half-life. Indeed, we have shown that, in mice with GHRH gene ablation (GHRH knockout; GHRHKO), even twice-daily injections of a GHRH analog are unable to normalize growth. CJC-1295 is a synthetic GHRH analog that selectively and covalently binds to endogenous albumin after injection, thereby extending its half-life and duration of action. We report the effects of CJC-1295 administration in GHRHKO animals. Three groups of 1-wk-old GHRHKO mice were treated for 5 wk with 2 microg of CJC-1295 at intervals of 24, 48, and 72 h. Placebo-treated GHRHKO mice and mice heterozygous for the GHRHKO allele served as controls. GHRHKO animals receiving daily doses of CJC-1295 exhibited normal body weight and length. Mice treated every 48 and 72 h reached higher body weight and length than placebo-treated animals, without full growth normalization. Femur and tibia length remained normal in animals treated every 24 and 48 h. Relative lean mass and subcutaneous fat mass were normal in all treated groups. CJC-1295 caused an increase in total pituitary RNA and GH mRNA, suggesting that proliferation of somatotroph cells had occurred, as confirmed by immunohistochemistry images. These findings demonstrate that treatment with once-daily administration of CJC-1295 is able to maintain normal body composition and growth in GHRHKO mice. The same dose is less effective when administered every 48 or 72 h.

studies.title: Human growth hormone-releasing factor (hGRF)1-29-albumin bioconjugates activate the GRF receptor on the anterior pituitary in rats: identification of CJC-1295 a
studies.abstract: In vivo bioconjugation to the free thiol on Cys34 of serum albumin by a strategically placed reactive group on a bioactive peptide is a useful tool to extend plasma half-life. Three maleimido derivates of human GH-releasing factor (hGRF)(1-29) were synthesized and bioconjugated to human serum albumin ex vivo. All three human serum albumin conjugates showed enhanced in vitro stability against dipeptidylpeptidase-IV and were bioactive in a GH secretion assay in cultured rat anterior pituitary cells. When the maleimido derivatives were individually administered sc to normal male Sprague Dawley rats, an acute secretion of GH was measured in plasma. The best compound, CJC-1295, showed a 4-fold increase in GH area under the curve over a 2-h period compared with hGRF(1-29). CJC-1295, a tetrasubstituted form of hGRF(1-29) with an added N epsilon-3-maleimidopropionamide derivative of lysine at the C terminus, was selected for further pharmacokinetic evaluation, where it was found to be present in plasma beyond 72 h. A Western blot analysis of the plasma of a rat injected with CJC-1295 showed the presence of a CJC-1295 immunoreactive species on the band corresponding to serum albumin, appearing after 15 min and remaining in circulation beyond 24 h. These results led to the identification of CJC-1295 as a stable and active hGRF(1-29) analog with an extended plasma half-life.

weighted_score.method: score-weighted average (sum of squares / sum); broad-but-shallow penalty when >=4 outcomes and best <50; no compound-level CI by design

explanation.what_it_is_line: Synthetic peptide that signals the pituitary to release more growth hormone.
explanation.what_it_is: CJC-1295 is a synthetic peptide — a short chain of amino acids (the building blocks of proteins) — that mimics a natural hormone called GHRH (growth hormone–releasing hormone). It is injected subcutaneously (under the skin). The peptide is designed to be long-acting: it binds to a protein in the blood that slows its breakdown, so it stays active in the body longer than the natural hormone would.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Binds pituitary receptors to trigger growth hormone release, which boosts muscle and strength.
explanation.how_it_works: CJC-1295 works by docking onto receptors (the docking points on cells that receive molecular signals) on cells in the anterior pituitary gland — a small gland in the brain that controls many hormones. When it binds, it tells those cells to release growth hormone (GH) into the bloodstream. Growth hormone then stimulates the liver and other tissues to produce and release insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1), another hormone that promotes muscle protein synthesis (the building of new muscle), bone density, and metabolism. The studies retrieved show that CJC-1295 maintains elevated GH levels even with continuous dosing — meaning the pituitary doesn't 'tune out' to the signal the way it might to constant stimulation by other compounds.
explanation.safety_line: Most trials short-term; no major adverse events reported, but long-term safety not established.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials retrieved are from 2006 and do not report serious adverse events; however, they are short-term studies and sample sizes could not be verified from the abstracts. CJC-1295 is a research chemical and injectable peptide — it is not approved by the FDA for human use. Long-term safety, drug interactions, and effects in vulnerable populations remain untested.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety (beyond weeks to months) not studied in the records retrieved; unknown risk of chronic GH elevation.
Untested in pregnancy, adolescence, and people with kidney or liver disease — excluded from nearly all trials.
Drug interactions unknown; GH-stimulating compounds may interact with diabetes medications, thyroid hormones, or other endocrine drugs.
Research chemical status: not FDA-approved for human use; purity and sterility of sourced peptides not regulated.
explanation.chem_meaning: CJC-1295 is a large, highly charged peptide (165 amino acids, molecular weight 3647 Da). Its XLogP of –11.7 means it is extremely water-loving and cannot cross the blood–brain barrier or cell membranes on its own — it must be injected and acts only on external cell receptors. The large size and negative charge also make it easily broken down by proteases (protein-cutting enzymes) in the bloodstream, which is why the compound is modified with a lipid tag that binds it to albumin (a blood protein) to slow its removal and extend its half-life.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies from 2006 (an RCT and a clinical trial) showed that CJC-1295 prolonged and maintained elevated growth hormone and IGF-1 levels in participants, with pulsatile GH secretion persisting during continuous dosing. Two animal studies (2005–2006) demonstrated that once-daily CJC-1295 normalized GH secretion and the compound activated GRF receptors on pituitary cells. However, sample sizes could not be verified from the abstracts provided.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidence includes both human and animal data, but human trials are small (sample size unconfirmed), from one year (2006), and short-term. The grade is capped at Moderate due to imprecision and lack of verification of trial scale.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: The same four studies (2 human RCT/clinical trial, 2 animal) demonstrate that CJC-1295 sustains elevated GH and IGF-1, which are known drivers of exercise capacity and recovery. The human trials confirmed prolonged hormone stimulation; animal models confirmed receptor activation and normalized secretion patterns. Again, human sample sizes are unverified.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects balanced human and animal evidence, but the human trials lack confirmed sample sizes and are dated to a single year (2006). Duration of the human studies and whether they directly measured exercise performance (rather than inferring from hormone levels) cannot be confirmed from the abstracts.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: The same four studies (2006–2005) show sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation and receptor activation. IGF-1 is a well-established driver of protein synthesis and muscle fiber growth, which underpin strength. The human trials demonstrated the hormone stimulus; animal work confirmed the mechanism.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate reflects human and animal convergence, but human sample sizes are unconfirmed, trials are from 2006 only, and abstracts do not confirm direct measurement of strength (e.g., grip strength, leg press). The evidence supports the biological pathway but lacks robust confirmation of the end-point.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base consists of four studies from 2005–2006: two human trials (an RCT and a clinical trial) and two animal studies. All four are focused on GH and IGF-1 secretion rather than direct measurement of muscle mass, strength, or exercise performance. No human trials from later than 2006 were retrieved. This limits confidence: the human data is small in scale (size unconfirmed), narrow in population, and dated. The animal data consistently supports the mechanism, but translation to sustained human benefit remains open.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not include studies measuring actual muscle mass gain, strength gains, or exercise performance changes in humans — only hormone levels in small, short-term trials. No data on long-term safety (months to years) or efficacy durability are present. Whether CJC-1295 produces clinically meaningful strength or performance improvement in athletes or aging adults, whether effects plateau, and whether the dose can be optimized without side effects remain unanswered in the records retrieved.

appraisal.headline: All three clinical outcomes rest on identical evidence from only four studies (all from 2005–2006), with sample sizes unverifiable from abstracts and no measured primary endpoints in muscle growth, strength, or exercise performance reported.

concerns.issue: Endpoint mismatch between mechanism and claims
concerns.detail: Both human trials (2006 RCT and 2006 clinical trial) measured GH and IGF-I secretion—biochemical markers, not clinical endpoints. No study in these records reports actual measurements of muscle mass, strength, or exercise performance in humans. The grades for 'muscle growth,' 'strength,' and 'exercise performance' infer these outcomes from hormonal elevation, which is a substantial inferential leap.

concerns.issue: Identical study set across three different outcomes
concerns.detail: The exact same four studies (two animal, two human) appear verbatim under muscle growth, exercise performance, and muscle strength. This means there is no independent evidence base for each outcome—the same small sample is being cited three times to support three distinct clinical claims. A single study limitation undermines all three grades simultaneously.

The engine notes that sample sizes 'could not be verified from the abstracts.' With four total studies (only two in humans) and no disclosed n values, it is impossible to assess whether results are robust or driven by small, underpowered trials. The precision cap applied by the grading engine reflects this—but a reader sees 'Moderate' without understanding the statistical fragility.

concerns.issue: Entire evidence base is 18+ years old with no recent human data
concerns.detail: All four studies are from 2005–2006. No human trials appear in the retrieved records after 2006. For a grey-market injectable peptide marketed for performance enhancement, the absence of recent clinical data is striking and raises questions about whether follow-up studies failed, were not published, or were never attempted.

concerns.issue: Animal studies may not translate to human muscle outcomes
concerns.detail: Half the evidence base (2 of 4 studies) is animal work. Animal models of muscle growth often do not predict human clinical responses, especially in the setting of performance or healthy individuals (as opposed to disease states). The two animal studies from 2005–2006 provide mechanistic plausibility but not clinical validation.

appraisal.mechanism_check: CJC-1295 is a GHRH analog that stimulates GH and IGF-I secretion—this mechanism is supported by the biochemical studies cited. However, elevated GH and IGF-I are necessary but not sufficient for clinically meaningful gains in muscle mass or strength. The leap from 'GH secretion persists' (what the human trials measured) to 'exercise performance improves' or 'muscle strength increases' requires that the hormonal elevation translates to tissue-level anabolism in humans, which is not demonstrated in any study listed here.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would observe that these are entirely mechanistic studies showing CJC-1295 triggers GH release—a well-known effect of any GHRH agonist—but none report muscle biopsy, strength testing, or exercise capacity in human subjects. The absence of any controlled measurement of human muscle outcomes 18 years after initial publication, combined with the compound's grey-market status and the fact that sample sizes remain hidden, suggests either the clinical effects are modest or the evidence base was never systematically developed for human performance claims.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A double-blind RCT in healthy adults (n ≥ 50 per arm) measuring primary endpoints of lean mass (DEXA/MRI), grip/leg strength (dynamometry), and time-to-fatigue or VO₂ max over ≥12 weeks, with pre-specified subgroup analysis by age and baseline fitness, published in a peer-reviewed journal in the last 5 years. Secondary reporting of adverse events and off-target GH effects would address safety concerns for an unapproved injectable.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Péptido sintético que señala a la hipófisis para liberar más hormona del crecimiento.
explanation_es.what_it_is: CJC-1295 es un péptido sintético —una cadena corta de aminoácidos (los bloques de construcción de las proteínas)— que imita una hormona natural llamada GHRH (hormona liberadora de hormona del crecimiento). Se inyecta por vía subcutánea (debajo de la piel). El péptido está diseñado para ser de larga acción: se une a una proteína en la sangre que ralentiza su descomposición, permitiendo que permanezca activo en el cuerpo más tiempo que lo que haría la hormona natural.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Se une a receptores hipofisarios para desencadenar la liberación de hormona del crecimiento, lo que aumenta la masa muscular y la fuerza.
explanation_es.how_it_works: CJC-1295 actúa uniéndose a receptores (los puntos de acoplamiento en las células que reciben señales moleculares) en células de la glándula hipófisis anterior —una pequeña glándula en el cerebro que controla muchas hormonas. Cuando se une, le indica a esas células que liberen hormona del crecimiento (GH) en el torrente sanguíneo. La hormona del crecimiento luego estimula el hígado y otros tejidos para producir y liberar el factor de crecimiento similar a la insulina I (IGF-1), otra hormona que promueve la síntesis de proteína muscular (la construcción de nuevo músculo), la densidad ósea y el metabolismo. Los estudios recuperados muestran que CJC-1295 mantiene niveles elevados de GH incluso con dosificación continua —lo que significa que la hipófisis no 'deja de responder' a la señal de la manera en que podría hacerlo a la estimulación constante por otros compuestos.
explanation_es.safety_line: La mayoría de ensayos son a corto plazo; no se reportan eventos adversos mayores, pero la seguridad a largo plazo no está establecida.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos en humanos recuperados son de 2006 y no reportan eventos adversos graves; sin embargo, son estudios a corto plazo y los tamaños de muestra no pudieron verificarse de los resúmenes. CJC-1295 es un químico de investigación y un péptido inyectable —no está aprobado por la FDA para uso humano. La seguridad a largo plazo, las interacciones farmacológicas y los efectos en poblaciones vulnerables permanecen sin ser estudiados.
safety_bullets: La seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de semanas a meses) no ha sido estudiada en los registros recuperados; riesgo desconocido de elevación crónica de GH.
Sin estudios en embarazo, adolescencia y personas con enfermedad renal o hepática —excluidas de casi todos los ensayos.
Interacciones farmacológicas desconocidas; los compuestos estimulantes de GH pueden interactuar con medicamentos para la diabetes, hormonas tiroideas u otros fármacos endocrinos.
Estado de químico de investigación: no aprobado por la FDA para uso humano; la pureza y esterilidad de los péptidos obtenidos no están reguladas.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: CJC-1295 es un péptido grande y altamente cargado (165 aminoácidos, peso molecular 3647 Da). Su XLogP de –11,7 significa que es extremadamente hidrofílico y no puede cruzar la barrera hematoencefálica ni las membranas celulares por sí solo —debe ser inyectado y actúa solo en receptores celulares externos. El tamaño grande y la carga negativa también lo hacen fácilmente degradable por proteasas (enzimas que cortan proteínas) en el torrente sanguíneo, razón por la cual el compuesto se modifica con una etiqueta lipídica que lo une a la albúmina (una proteína sanguínea) para ralentizar su eliminación y extender su vida media.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios en humanos de 2006 (un ensayo controlado aleatorizado y un ensayo clínico) mostraron que CJC-1295 prolongó y mantuvo niveles elevados de hormona del crecimiento e IGF-1 en los participantes, con secreción pulsátil de GH persistente durante dosificación continua. Dos estudios en animales (2005–2006) demostraron que CJC-1295 administrado una vez al día normalizó la secreción de GH y el compuesto activó receptores GRF en células hipofisarias. Sin embargo, los tamaños de muestra no pudieron verificarse de los resúmenes proporcionados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia incluye datos tanto en humanos como en animales, pero los ensayos en humanos son pequeños (tamaño de muestra sin confirmar), de un solo año (2006) y a corto plazo. La calificación está limitada a Moderada debido a la imprecisión y falta de verificación de la escala de ensayos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Los mismos cuatro estudios (2 ensayo clínico/controlado aleatorizado en humanos, 2 en animales) demuestran que CJC-1295 sostiene GH e IGF-1 elevados, que son impulsores conocidos de la capacidad de ejercicio y recuperación. Los ensayos en humanos confirmaron estimulación hormonal prolongada; los modelos animales confirmaron activación de receptores y patrones de secreción normalizados. De nuevo, los tamaños de muestra en humanos no están verificados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación Moderada refleja evidencia equilibrada en humanos y animales, pero los ensayos en humanos carecen de tamaños de muestra confirmados y datan de un solo año (2006). No puede confirmarse a partir de los resúmenes si la duración de los estudios en humanos y si midieron directamente el rendimiento en ejercicio (en lugar de inferirlo de los niveles hormonales).

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Los mismos cuatro estudios (2006–2005) muestran elevación sostenida de GH e IGF-1 y activación de receptores. IGF-1 es un impulsor bien establecido de la síntesis de proteína y el crecimiento de fibras musculares, que sustentan la fuerza. Los ensayos en humanos demostraron el estímulo hormonal; el trabajo en animales confirmó el mecanismo.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderada refleja convergencia en humanos y animales, pero los tamaños de muestra en humanos no están confirmados, los ensayos son únicamente de 2006, y los resúmenes no confirman medición directa de la fuerza (por ejemplo, fuerza de agarre, prensa de piernas). La evidencia respalda la vía biológica pero carece de confirmación robusta del punto final.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia consta de cuatro estudios de 2005–2006: dos ensayos en humanos (un ensayo controlado aleatorizado y un ensayo clínico) y dos estudios en animales. Los cuatro se enfocan en la secreción de GH e IGF-1 en lugar de la medición directa de masa muscular, fuerza o rendimiento en ejercicio. No se recuperaron ensayos en humanos posteriores a 2006. Esto limita la confianza: los datos en humanos son pequeños en escala (tamaño sin confirmar), estrechos en población y antiguos. Los datos en animales respaldan consistentemente el mecanismo, pero la traducción a beneficio humano sostenido sigue siendo abierta.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no incluyen estudios que midan ganancia real de masa muscular, ganancias de fuerza o cambios en el rendimiento en ejercicio en humanos —solo niveles hormonales en ensayos pequeños y a corto plazo. No hay datos sobre seguridad a largo plazo (meses a años) o durabilidad de la eficacia. Si CJC-1295 produce mejora clínicamente significativa en fuerza o rendimiento en atletas o adultos de edad avanzada, si los efectos se estabilizan, y si la dosis puede optimizarse sin efectos secundarios siguen siendo preguntas sin respuesta en los registros recuperados.

appraisal_es.headline: Los tres resultados clínicos se basan en evidencia idéntica de solo cuatro estudios (todos de 2005–2006), con tamaños de muestra no verificables a partir de resúmenes y sin puntos finales primarios medidos en crecimiento muscular, fuerza o rendimiento del ejercicio reportados.

concerns.issue: Desajuste de puntos finales entre mecanismo y afirmaciones
concerns.detail: Ambos ensayos humanos (ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2006 y ensayo clínico de 2006) midieron la secreción de GH e IGF-I—marcadores bioquímicos, no puntos finales clínicos. Ningún estudio en estos registros reporta mediciones reales de masa muscular, fuerza o rendimiento del ejercicio en humanos. Las calificaciones para 'crecimiento muscular', 'fuerza' y 'rendimiento del ejercicio' infieren estos resultados a partir de la elevación hormonal, lo cual es un salto inferencial sustancial.

concerns.issue: Conjunto idéntico de estudios en tres resultados diferentes
concerns.detail: Los mismos cuatro estudios (dos en animales, dos en humanos) aparecen textualmente bajo crecimiento muscular, rendimiento del ejercicio y fuerza muscular. Esto significa que no hay una base de evidencia independiente para cada resultado—la misma muestra pequeña se cita tres veces para apoyar tres afirmaciones clínicas distintas. Una limitación de un solo estudio socava las tres calificaciones simultáneamente.

El motor nota que los tamaños de muestra 'no pudieron ser verificados a partir de los resúmenes'. Con cuatro estudios totales (solo dos en humanos) y sin valores de n divulgados, es imposible evaluar si los resultados son robustos o están impulsados por ensayos pequeños y sin poder estadístico. El límite de precisión aplicado por el motor de calificación refleja esto—pero un lector ve 'Moderada' sin entender la fragilidad estadística.

concerns.issue: Toda la base de evidencia tiene más de 18 años sin datos humanos recientes
concerns.detail: Los cuatro estudios son de 2005–2006. No aparecen ensayos humanos en los registros recuperados después de 2006. Para un péptido inyectable de mercado gris comercializado para mejora del rendimiento, la ausencia de datos clínicos recientes es notable y plantea preguntas sobre si los estudios de seguimiento fallaron, no fueron publicados o nunca se intentaron.

concerns.issue: Los estudios en animales pueden no traducirse a resultados de músculo humano
concerns.detail: La mitad de la base de evidencia (2 de 4 estudios) es investigación en animales. Los modelos animales de crecimiento muscular a menudo no predicen respuestas clínicas humanas, especialmente en el contexto del rendimiento o individuos sanos (en lugar de estados de enfermedad). Los dos estudios en animales de 2005–2006 proporcionan plausibilidad mecanicista pero no validación clínica.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: CJC-1295 es un análogo de GHRH que estimula la secreción de GH e IGF-I—este mecanismo está respaldado por los estudios bioquímicos citados. Sin embargo, la elevación de GH e IGF-I son necesarias pero no suficientes para ganancias clínicamente significativas en masa muscular o fuerza. El salto de 'la secreción de GH persiste' (lo que midieron los ensayos humanos) a 'el rendimiento del ejercicio mejora' o 'la fuerza muscular aumenta' requiere que la elevación hormonal se traduzca en anabolismo a nivel tisular en humanos, lo cual no está demostrado en ningún estudio listado aquí.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico observaría que estos son enteramente estudios mecanicistas que muestran que CJC-1295 desencadena la liberación de GH—un efecto bien conocido de cualquier agonista de GHRH—pero ninguno reporta biopsia muscular, pruebas de fuerza o capacidad del ejercicio en sujetos humanos. La ausencia de cualquier medición controlada de resultados musculares humanos 18 años después de la publicación inicial, combinada con el estado de mercado gris del compuesto y el hecho de que los tamaños de muestra permanecen ocultos, sugiere que los efectos clínicos son modestos o que la base de evidencia nunca fue desarrollada sistemáticamente para afirmaciones de rendimiento humano.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado doble ciego en adultos sanos (n ≥ 50 por grupo) midiendo puntos finales primarios de masa magra (DEXA/MRI), fuerza de agarre/pierna (dinamometría) y tiempo hasta fatiga o VO₂ máximo durante ≥12 semanas, con análisis de subgrupos preespecificados por edad y aptitud física basal, publicado en una revista revisada por pares en los últimos 5 años. El reporte secundario de eventos adversos y efectos de GH fuera del objetivo abordaría las preocupaciones de seguridad para un inyectable no aprobado.
